Hai, let me think through this year. I'm 70 now, and honestly I don't know that much about farming yet. My son went to the city to work in the factory last year, and the 6 mu came to me. Before that I mostly did other things — I never paid much attention to the fields. So I'm just following what Old Wang next door does, and sometimes my cousin comes over and tells me what to do. The young fellow at the 供销社 (supply shop) in town also tells me what fertilizer to buy when I go in.

Let me go through each piece.

**The wheat** — already in the ground. I planted about 3 mu of it back in October, same plot where I'll grow maize after. When I planted, I put down one bag of that compound stuff (the 15-15-15 kind, what everyone buys) per mu, mixed in before drilling. Come spring — March or early April when the wheat greens up and starts to joint — I'll scatter half a bag of urea per mu. That's what Old Wang told me. If it looks a bit yellow I'll put a little more, but urea is expensive so I watch. Water it maybe 3 times — once when it wakes up from winter, once at jointing, once when the heads come out. The well is ours, just the electricity costs. Won't spray unless I see problems or the neighbors all spray — then I'll do what they do. I hope for 400 kg per mu. My family eats some, the rest I sell.

**The maize** — goes in right after wheat comes off in June. That week is very tight, no time to plow. I just direct-seed into the stubble. I buy hybrid seed from the shop — the young man there picks it for me. One bag of compound at planting per mu, and maybe a bit of urea later if the stalks look weak. Water once or twice if the rain doesn't come. Maize is easier on my back than wheat. Hope for 450 kg per mu.

**The cotton** — 2 mu on the other plot. This is the hard one. My back hurts already thinking about it. I plant end of April. My wife helps, and when it's picking time my daughter-in-law comes back from the town to help for a few weeks. One bag compound when I plant, then a little urea when it flowers. Water a couple times. The bollworms — I have to spray several times, my cousin tells me when. Cotton price has been low, I'm not sure if it's worth it, but what else would I plant on that piece? I don't know any other crops.

**The stevia** — 1 mu. I only do it because the company came to the village two years ago and they give you the seedlings and tell you what to do, then they come and collect the leaves. Steady money. I don't need to think much, I just follow what they say.

Altogether I figure about 2,700 yuan for inputs this year. My son sends some money from the city and my youngest works at the brick factory, so we get by. I can't afford to be fancy — whatever is on sale at the 供销社 is what I buy. If fertilizer goes up I use a little less. Simple as that.
